correctness.rationale: The final no-child event is the intersection of independent exclusions of one parent label at every subsequent arrival. Conditioning preserves the independence and uniformity of eligible parents. The exact conditional recurrence has solution \(\mathbb E[T_k\mid X_{n,j}=1]-\mathbb E[T_k]=-(H_{k-1}-H_{j-1})\) for every \(j\le k\le n\). Multiplication by (j-1)/(n-1) proves the covariance. Reversing two finite sums gives \(-(n-2)/4\). The adjacent-difference formula is strictly decreasing, and the bulk harmonic limit peaks at \(e^{-1}\). Independent exact enumeration of all 46,233 trees through nine vertices and conditional recurrence checks through 159 vertices passed. Computation checks are finite and not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The proposed contribution is the full birth-indexed leaf/no-child conditioning regression and covariance profile, not the known distribution of total path length or marginal leaves. A full reading of the classical 1999 path-length paper showed univariate moment recurrences and no vertex-marked leaf covariance. A later full-text four-variable generating function marks only global leaf count and path lengths; deriving the aggregate covariance from it would not supply the indexed formula. A related root-attachment/path-length result concerns a different event and does not determine the higher-order no-attachment event. Earlier indexed mixed-moment coverage is not conclusively excluded; the risk is explicitly recorded.

value.rationale: The particular statistic is motivated by the age of a vertex in a recursive growth model: being childless becomes less likely with age, while its effect on overall path length grows with remaining exposure time. The exact conditional shift, negative covariance for every eligible birth index, strict finite concavity and unique limiting maximizing age \(e^{-1}\) give a complete natural local dependence profile. Summation yields the aggregate path-length/leaf-count covariance; this is a structural connection, rather than a toy finite table or arbitrary slice.
